newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel - Romanian demand lurks, low sulphur busy.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel - Romanian demand lurks, low sulphur busy.

text.p: Fuel oil saw a volatile day price- wise on Thursday with the market moving according to the latest trade. Overall the sector remained buoyant with Romanian demand now starting to impact.
High sulphur barges gained up to $3 a tonne in the morning, with deals at $125/$126 fob ARA, but the rise was not sustained and trade was done later at $124 and the market put at $122-124.

A high sulphur cargo was sold at $115.50 for a short into the U.K. "The buyer needed the cargo more than the seller had to sell," said one trader who viewed the prices as high in relation to barge swaps of $120-121.

But others said it reflected the market. Unconfirmed talk of a cargo sold at $129 cif Romania was welcomed by the bulls. "It will impact the Med first then NWE later," said one. Romania has announced it will buy up to 1.2 million tonnes this winter.
Low sulphur cracked cargoes settled unchanged around $135 cif Med with the main Med buyer picking up its third cargo this week at $135.50 cif Milazzo.
Traders agreed that Wednesday's trade at $133 fob Med had been overplayed. The sector was firm, but not overly tight with several large pieces still available.
